`case_study:apple-2016-2023-buffett` · tickers US-AAPL · confidence: verified

Berkshire (Combs/Weschler first, then Buffett) started buying in Q1 2016 when Apple traded ~$90-110 pre-2020-split (~$23-27 today) at ~10-11x earnings, ~9x ex-cash, priced as a peaking hardware cyclical after the first iPhone unit decline. Cost: ~$31.1bn for 908m shares (~$34/share avg) per Berkshire. End-2023 ~$198: ~8x from 2016 low, stake worth ~$170bn+. Split [my arithmetic, approx]: EPS ~$2.08 (FY16, adj) -> ~$6.13 (FY23) ≈ 2.9x, helped by ~40% share-count reduction via buybacks; P/E ~11x -> ~30x ≈ 2.8x. So roughly half EPS, half rerating. Drawdowns: Oct 2018-Jan 2019 ~-39%; COVID 2020 ~-31%; 2022 ~-31%. EARLY SIGNAL in 2016: very high retention/upgrade loyalty, Services revenue growing ~20%+ on an installed base >1bn devices, net cash ~$150bn+ funding buybacks, at a market-level multiple. Who caught it: Warren Buffett / Berkshire (documented 13F, letters). Ended: Berkshire sold ~13% in Q1 2024 and ~390m shares in Q2 2024 (~2/3 of stake by late 2024) as P/E reached ~30x with EPS growth single-digit. LESSON: the biggest gain often comes from the market reclassifying a business (cyclical hardware -> consumer franchise/Services toll); once rerated, future returns fall to EPS growth and the same investor may rationally sell.

- **Start → end:** ~$23-27 split-adj (2016) → ~$198 (Dec 2023) (~8x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** ~50/50: EPS x2.9 (buybacks), P/E x2.8
- **Max drawdown:** -39% (2018-19)
- **Early signal:** 10x P/E, Services growth, installed base, buyback capacity
- **Who caught it:** Berkshire Hathaway (Buffett, Combs, Weschler)
- **Ended/stalled:** Berkshire sold ~2/3 in 2024 at ~30x P/E
- **Lesson:** reclassification rerating; sell discipline when multiple is full
- **Sources:** [1](https://fortune.com/2024/08/03/warren-buffett-berkshire-hathaway-q2-earnings-report-stock-sales-apple-stake/) · [2](https://fortune.com/2024/05/04/warren-buffett-berkshire-hathaway-brkb-brka-q1-earnings-apple-stock-sale/) · [3](https://www.irishtimes.com/business/2024/02/15/warren-buffetts-berkshire-hathaway-reduces-its-stake-in-apple) · [4](https://appleinsider.com/articles/24/08/03/berkshire-hathaway-unloaded-more-than-half-of-its-apple-stock-last-quarter)

`case_study:india-psu-rally-2023-24` | confidence: **verified** | tags: india, rerating, sector-psu, sector-defence, sector-railways, cyclical

The BSE PSU index rose ~5x from March 2020 to mid-2024 on government capex (~Rs 6 to ~9.5 lakh crore) and a narrative shift from 'value traps' to 'nation-building' stocks. Railway names (RVNL, IRFC) and defence/shipbuilding (Mazagon Dock, Cochin Shipyard, HAL, BEL) posted triple-digit gains; IRFC, a government lender, traded at a large multiple of book and RVNL, a contractor, at high P/Es (levels unverified). Business Standard (2023) found the rally was mainly multiple rerating; in Apr 2025 defence forward P/Es were ~2x their history (HAL ~28x vs ~14x; BEL ~41x vs ~21x). Peak: July 2024. Unwind: BSE CPSE index ~-30% from the July 2024 peak by end-Feb 2025; Mazagon Dock -59% and Cochin Shipyard -52% from July 2024; by late 2025 IRFC, Concor and RVNL were ~-46% and IRCTC ~-40%. The 4 June 2024 election result (no single-party majority) was an early crack (sharp one-day PSU fall, from memory). Defence had sharp rebounds in 2025 (geopolitics), railways briefly in Sept/Dec 2025. Top signals: valuations ~2x history with no matching earnings upgrade, heavy retail and thematic-fund ownership, government OFS selling into strength, high-stake PSUs (82-89% government) with tiny free floats. Lesson: rerating rallies end when multiples hit the ceiling, even when the capex story continues.

| key | value |
|---|---|
| run | BSE PSU ~5x Mar 2020-Jul 2024 |
| peak | Jul 2024 |
| drawdown | CPSE ~-30% by Feb 2025; MDL -59%; railways ~-46% |
| valuation | ~2x historical P/E |
| lesson | rerating ceilings end rallies |

body:
**Part B — systematic universe test (pre-registered here).** Universe = the 580 usable companies of the
PEAD sample (`research_notes/Backtests/india_pead.md` §1: seeded random sample of the current NSE EQ/BE
list → survivors only). Snapshot **T0 = 30-Sep-2020**; fundamentals FY2016–FY2020 (screener consolidated if
it has ≥3 of those years, else standalone); pledge from the BSE SHP for March 2020; auditor resignations
from NSE corporate announcements 1-Jan-2015 → 30-Sep-2020. Mechanical rules:
- **R1** Σ5y CFO / Σ5y PAT < 0.3 (PAT sum > 0, non-lender); **R1b** same < 0.7
- **R2** promoter pledge > 25% of promoter holding (Mar-2020); **R2b** > 50%
- **R3** any statutory-auditor resignation announced before T0 (internal/secretarial/cost/branch excluded)
- **R4** borrowings FY20 ≥ 1.5x FY17 and Σ CFO FY18–20 < 0 (non-lender)
- **R5** other income / PBT (FY18–20) > 30% (PBT > 0, non-lender) — reported separately
- **ANY** = R1 or R2 or R3 or R4

Outcomes: adjusted close on the first trading day on/after T0 vs the first on/after 30-Sep-2025 (5 years;
last close if the series stops earlier) and vs 18-Nov-2026 (to date). Events: **loss50** = ratio < 0.5,
**x3** = ratio > 3. Report P(event | flagged) vs P(event | unflagged) and the base rate, Wilson 95% CIs,
two-sided Fisher exact p. **Decision rules (fixed now):** a rule "earns its place" as a hard filter only if
flagged→loss50 is at least 2x the base rate with Fisher p < 0.05 **and** flagged→x3 is not above the base
rate; a rule whose flagged→x3 rate is ≥ the base rate is not a hard filter whatever its loss rate.
Known biases, stated in advance: (1) survivors-only universe (firms delisted before mid-2023 are absent, which
removes exactly the worst traps, so loss rates for flagged firms are understated); (2) screener figures are
current/restated, not as-first-reported; (3) 2020-09 → 2025-09 was a strong small/mid-cap bull market, so x3
base rates are high and loss50 base rates low; (4) one snapshot, ~500 firms: power is low for rare flags.

body:
**5.1 Materials basket FY26 vs FY25 `[AR26 n.26a]` (₹ cr):** iron ore 481 (507), coke 433 (581), ferro alloys 384 (376), **coking coal 376
(140)**, coal 130 (151), others 302 (326), fluxes 106 (100), scrap/HBI 81 (8), electrodes 33, super-alloy RM 26 (10).
- **Carbon basket (coke + coking coal + coal) = ₹939 cr = 23.8% of sales ≈ ₹18,900/t of liquid steel.** A 10% move in the price of the carbon basket = ±₹94 cr ≈ **±240 bps
  of OPM**. This is the top micro-driver. The FY26 mix shift from coke to coking coal (+₹236 cr coking coal, −₹148 cr coke) suggests own coke/PCI
  usage changed. That is a question for the plant visit.
- **Iron ore ₹481 cr ≈ 12.2% of sales.** Hot metal 471.7k t × ~1.6 t ore/t ≈ 0.75 Mt ore → ~₹6,400/t delivered [EST]. A 10% ore move = ±₹48 cr ≈ ±120 bps.
  LMEL's Surjagarh ore (Gadchiroli) is the nearest large source. Supplier names are not disclosed, so whether Sunflag buys from LMEL is unknown.
- **Ferro alloys ₹384 cr (9.7%)**: SBQ grades need Cr/Mn/Mo/Ni. Alloy prices are a leading series (alloy surcharges are passed through with a lag).
- **Pass-through.** SBQ prices to forgers/OEMs are reset quarterly or monthly (industry practice, [EST]), so OPM lags the carbon basket by ~1 quarter. Leading
  series: SGX/Platts coking coal, Indian met-coke prices (BigMint), Odisha/Chhattisgarh iron-ore lump (NMDC price notices are dated and public).

**5.2 Power: 6.9% of sales.** Purchased electricity = 137.75 m kWh renewable (3x FY25, from the ReNew JV) + 329.3 m kWh grid `[AR26 BRSR P6]`, total 467 m kWh, + 157.7 m kWh captive.
Cost per purchased kWh ≈ ₹270 cr ÷ 467 m ≈ **₹5.8/kWh**. Intensity ≈ 1,335 kWh per t rolled (all electricity). **Sensitivity:** ±₹0.50/kWh on
purchased power = ±₹23 cr ≈ ±60 bps. MSEDCL tariff orders (MERC) are the dated, leading document. The renewable share rose from 10% to 30% and
lowered the grid bill, which is one reason FY26 OPM beat FY25.

**5.3 People: not a micro-driver.** 1,318 permanent staff plus 2,702 contract workers; **1,716 contract workers (63.5%) are paid exactly the minimum wage** `[AR26
BRSR P5]`. Wage pool indexed to the notification ≈ 1,716 × ~₹15k/month × 12 × 1.29 load ≈ ₹40 cr [EST]. A 10% minimum-wage step ≈ ₹4 cr ≈ 10 bps.
The contract-expense line is ₹223 cr (+22% YoY) and is the bigger watch item. Median worker pay is ₹8.37 lakh; the MD earns 41x the median.
